meta.title: Delaware Department of Justice Outside Counsel Billing Policy (bid JUD-DOJ25001)
meta.licence: No licence stated. Government/public-institution publication posted on the open web; used only as a public document for internal evaluation, not redistributed.
meta.pii_note: Public document from an agency or court; counts only, no matched text recorded. No pattern hits. Hits are agency contact details, addresses and generic role words, not private individuals.

pii_scan.disposition: Business and agency contact details only; no private-person data expected. Safe for local evaluation use.

rules.paraphrase: Rates stay fixed for the matter; a change needs written approval 60 days before it takes effect.
Invoices are rendered monthly within 30 days after month end, for the whole month, with no carry-over billing across months.
Invoices reference matter and invoice number and list per-timekeeper time with date, activity, subject and persons involved; insufficient narrative is rejected.
Entries are in tenths of an hour, no less than 0.1; tasks totalling a de minimis amount may be combined up to 0.5 hours a day.
Block billing and entries such as bare 'Research' or 'Telephone calls' are unacceptable.
No more than two attorneys at meetings, depositions, mediations, negotiations or hearings, no paralegals at them, and no summer intern or clerk time without pre-approval.
More than ten hours a day by one person is closely reviewed.
Time spent preparing, reviewing or correcting invoices is not acceptable; secretarial time and staff overtime are not permitted.
Internal conferences above 10 percent of monthly billing, general-knowledge research, duplicative work and excess file review are closely reviewed.
Overhead items, online research, fax/phone, in-state transportation, meals and any markup are not reimbursed.
Photocopies at most ten cents a page; every disbursement is itemised by units, unit price and total, and grouped or miscellaneous lines may be refused.
Out-of-state travel, expedited or multiple transcripts and outside experts or contract attorneys need prior approval.

unmapped_provisions.paraphrase: Attorney time for paralegal or clerical tasks, and senior rates for work a junior could do, are closely reviewed.
The State does not negotiate prompt-pay discounts and pays no late fees.
